paragraphs.source_en:
Apollo
35 And I shall gaze not on the deeds which make
My mind obscure with sorrow, as eclipse
Darkens the sphere I guide — but list, I hear
The small, clear, silver lute of the young Spirit
That sits i’ the morning star.

paragraphs.source_en:
Ocean
Thou must away?
 40 Thy steeds will pause at even — till when, farewell.
 The loud deep calls me home even now to feed it
With azure calm out of the emerald urns
Which stand forever full beside my throne.
 Behold the Nereids under the green sea,
45 Their wavering limbs borne on the wind-like streams,

light-laden] Nbk 9 (alt. from unladen), perhaps with a pun on ‘lightly laden’ and ‘laden with light’;
light laden 1820, 1839.
 ‘A star above the tip of a new moon suggests a boat guided by an invisible (sightless) pilot with a
star as his crest’ (Butter (1970)).
 Another reference to the conditions of naval service and warfare, and to the slave trade.
 groans] Nbk 9; groans, 1820, 1839.
 command —] Nbk 9; command; 1820, 1839.
 free] Written above frank canc. in Nbk 9.
 eclipse] Eclipse Nbk 9.
 guide —] Nbk 9; guide; 1820, 1839.
 See Curran (1975) 59–60 for commentary on the symbolic patterning of morning and evening
stars in PU.
 i’ the] Nbk 9 (S. has canc. the n of in), 1839; on the 1820, 1829; probably in S.’s errata list. morning]
Morning Nbk 9. away?] Nbk 9; away; 1820, 1839.
